CVE-2026-92392.why: HTTP/2 upload use-after-free when the server resets the stream (curl 8.21.0 to 8.22.0, fixed in 8.23.0). Needs a request with a body over HTTPS/HTTP2 to a malicious or compromised server. The base's libcurl users (git, nix, systemd, NetworkManager, elfutils, tpm2-tss) and TAPPaaS's curl calls upload only to TAPPaaS's own services and to the code forges over TLS. Fix: curl 8.23.0, in staging-next-26.05, not yet on the nixos-26.05 channel.

CVE-2026-6507.why: A dnsmasq DHCP server with --dhcp-split-relay; dnsmasq is only a NetworkManager dependency on guests and does not run.

CVE-2026-62960.why: Git for Windows only (transport_get_remote_bundle_uri in the Windows port); guests run git on Linux.

CVE-2019-1010022.why: Disputed upstream: a stack-guard bypass that needs an overflow already exploited; the record names no affected versions. Unchanged in glibc 2.42-103. Kept counted, as glibc is.

CVE-2019-1010023.why: Disputed upstream: ldd run on a malicious ELF, which glibc treats as a non-security bug; the record names no affected versions. Unchanged in glibc 2.42-103. Kept counted, as glibc is.

CVE-2026-84243.why: gettext loads a catalog from a LANGUAGE value containing / or ..; it needs an attacker who sets LANGUAGE for a program running with other rights and without AT_SECURE. On the guests nobody outside can: sshd accepts no client environment (AcceptEnv unset, forgejo only GIT_PROTOCOL; PermitUserEnvironment no; checked on all NixOS guests on hrossen 2026-11-07), services get fixed systemd environments, and sudo is setuid (AT_SECURE). Admins who log in already run code as themselves.

CVE-2025-32990.why: In certtool's template parsing; certtool is not run on guests.

CVE-2026-1584.why: A TLS server's PSK handshake; only NetworkManager loads gnutls on a guest, as a client, and no guest serves TLS through gnutls.

CVE-2026-33845.why: DTLS handshake reassembly; nothing on a guest speaks DTLS through gnutls.

CVE-2026-3833.why: nameConstraints in X.509 path validation through gnutls; the only gnutls user on a guest (NetworkManager) does no such validation for TAPPaaS (wired, no 802.1X).

CVE-2026-42009.why: DTLS packet reordering; nothing on a guest speaks DTLS through gnutls.

CVE-2026-42010.why: A TLS server with RSA-PSK; no guest serves TLS through gnutls.

CVE-2026-4878.why: A TOCTOU in cap_set_file needing a local user with write access to the parent directory; only root runs setcap, at activation.

CVE-2026-118374.why: Memory exhaustion in LibreSSL's ocspcheck tool from a malicious OCSP responder; ocspcheck is not on any guest's PATH, nothing runs it, and no running process maps libressl (checked on all NixOS guests on hrossen 2026-11-07).

CVE-2026-55199.why: Needs the client to connect to a malicious SSH server; libssh2's users on a guest (NetworkManager, nix-daemon) open no SSH connections (nix fetches over HTTPS).

CVE-2026-55200.why: Malicious SSH server against a libssh2 client; no guest opens SSH connections through libssh2.

CVE-2026-58050.why: publickey subsystem of a malicious SSH server, 32-bit only; no guest opens SSH connections through libssh2.

CVE-2008-3844.why: Trojaned Red Hat Enterprise Linux 4/5 OpenSSH packages signed in August 2008; matched by product name only. NixOS builds upstream OpenSSH.

CVE-2026-3497.why: Affects the GSSAPI patch some Linux distributions add, not upstream OpenSSH; nixpkgs' default openssh carries no GSSAPI patch, and GSSAPI authentication is off.

CVE-2026-106553.why: sshd keeping GSSAPI credentials after a failed GSSAPIAuthentication attempt. nixpkgs builds openssh without Kerberos (withKerberos = false: no --with-kerberos5, no krb5 in its closure), so sshd has no GSSAPI authentication at all: sshd -T lists no GSSAPI option. Every NixOS guest and the mothership run that one build (43zp0r...-openssh-10.5p1). Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6.

CVE-2026-106555.why: sshd keeping GSSAPI authentication state across attempts. nixpkgs builds openssh without Kerberos (withKerberos = false: no --with-kerberos5, no krb5 in its closure), so sshd has no GSSAPI authentication at all: sshd -T lists no GSSAPI option. Every NixOS guest and the mothership run that one build (43zp0r...-openssh-10.5p1). Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6.

CVE-2026-106583.why: ssh client: a $ or \ in a command-line username is injected where %r/%u is expanded into a shell-run directive (ProxyCommand, LocalCommand, Match exec). The guests' ssh_config has only systemd's ssh proxy, whose ProxyCommand uses %h and %p, the operator's ~/.ssh/config none, and TAPPaaS calls ssh with fixed user names (tappaas, root). Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6.

CVE-2023-51767.why: Rowhammer flip of the authenticated flag in mm_answer_authpassword (disputed upstream), the PasswordAuthentication path; every NixOS guest runs sshd with PasswordAuthentication no, and no account has a usable password hash, so keyboard-interactive/PAM cannot authenticate by password either (sshd -T and /etc/shadow checked on all 19 NixOS guests on hrossen 2026-11-07).

CVE-2026-13221.why: Regexes with more than 65535 alternation branches; perl on a guest runs only NixOS's own scripts, with no attacker-supplied pattern.

CVE-2026-57432.why: pack/unpack templates from an attacker; perl on a guest runs only NixOS's own scripts.

CVE-2026-8376.why: Regex compilation on 32-bit builds; guests are x86_64 and run only NixOS's own perl scripts.

CVE-2026-119741.why: Sender-side hash_search DoS by a malicious receiver pulling from a public rsync daemon module; no guest runs an rsync daemon (nothing listens on 873, checked on all NixOS guests on hrossen 2026-11-07), and rsync over ssh only runs between TAPPaaS hosts.

CVE-2026-11822.why: A crafted FTS5 database supplied by an attacker; sqlite on a guest opens only nix's own root-owned database.

CVE-2026-53613.why: Non-root mount(8) TOCTOU, reachable only through an /etc/fstab entry with the user or users option; no guest's fstab has one (checked on all 19 NixOS guests on hrossen 2026-11-07) and no module declares one. 2.42.4 also closes it except for the legacy mount(2) path without /proc, which no guest uses.
